newsitem.title: CANADA: Rigel keeps shining after North Sea news.
newsitem.headline: Rigel keeps shining after North Sea news.

text.p: Shares of Calgary-based Rigel Energy Corp continued their rise on Thursday after the company's chief executive provided details of what could be a major oil find in the U.K. North Sea.
Rigel, which had been rumored as a takeover target, was up 0.65 to 17.40 -- a new 52-week high -- in Toronto Stock Exchange trade. It rose to 17.70 earlier in Thursday's session.

Rigel's Don West told the company's annual meeting on Wednesday that the Moray Firth discovery, in which the firm holds 20 percent, could hold up to 900 million barrels of oil in place with a recovery factor of 30-40 percent.
Britain's BG Plc holds 50 percent of the play and Amerada Hess Corp has 30 percent.

The discovery well off the east coast of Scotland tested at 2,600 barrels a day in early May, although West said it could have flowed four or five times that amount if not for mechanical problems during the test. An appraisal well is planned for later this year.
West said full development could cost a total of US$1 billion and the company could pay out its share in 2-1/2 years if the field meets expectations.
BG later declined to comment on West's predictions.

Rigel, whose shares have climbed from 13.45 on May 2, may still be a potential bid target, but the discovery and other plays that could have a big impact on reserves would make it a lot more expensive, West said.

"If somebody wants to pay the price, I guess, who am I to stand in the way?" he told reporters on Wednesday. "But what I'm trying to get through is the share price better be pretty substancial with what I'm showing you. And it's not 16 bucks."
